page: Microsoft Azure M416s_10_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, designed for workloads requiring massive memory capacity and high core counts. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 416 dedicated vCPUs derived from 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 9496.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 22.83 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with 4194 GB of capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25% category. However, the massive core count enables top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with uncached read speeds reaching 695.9 GB/sec and write speeds at 319.92 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at a top-tier level of 247.68 million operations per second, though Passmark memory latency tests score in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents an ultra-high-density resource profile. The extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio and massive scale make it a specialized option for large-scale enterprise databases, in-memory analytics, and heavy multi-threaded workloads. While single-threaded tasks are inefficient on this hardware, the server is highly optimized for massive parallel processing, large-scale Redis deployments, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure M416s_10_v2 is an ultra-high-density, memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family. It features 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores, 9496.0 GB of RAM, and 4194 GB of local storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance is designed for massive parallel processing. Benchmark results show a significant tradeoff: single-core performance is weak, falling in the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core CPU performance, uncached memory bandwidth, and Redis SET operations rank in the top 10% tier. With approximately 22.83 GB of RAM per core, this server is qualitatively structured for extreme memory-intensive applications. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, high-throughput data processing, and massive multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
